title: Peak versus average sunlight

Its converter outputs 80% of incident power but clips electrical output at 320 W. Calculate daily electrical energy, identifying when clipping begins for a symmetric day, and check against the unclipped upper bound.

answer:
Take noon as \(t=0\), with sunlight from \(t=-5\) h to \(t=+5\) h. The incident power is the triangular profile

\[
P_{\rm in}(t)=600\left(1-\frac{|t|}{5}\right)\ \text{W},\qquad |t|\le 5.
\]

The converter output before clipping is

\[
P_{\rm out,unclipped}=0.8P_{\rm in}
=480\left(1-\frac{|t|}{5}\right)\ \text{W}.
\]

Clipping occurs when this reaches \(320\) W:

\[
480\left(1-\frac{|t|}{5}\right)=320
\]

\[
1-\frac{|t|}{5}=\frac{2}{3}
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
|t|=\frac{5}{3}\ {\rm h}=1\ {\rm h}\ 40\ {\rm min}.
\]

Thus clipping begins at \(1{:}40\) before noon, i.e. **10:20 AM**, and ends at **1:40 PM**.

The daily clipped electrical energy is

\[
E=\int_{-5}^{5}\min\{0.8P_{\rm in}(t),320\}\,dt
\]

\[
E=2\left[
320\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)
+\int_{5/3}^{5}96(5-t)\,dt
\right]
\]

\[
E=\frac{6400}{3}\ {\rm Wh}
=2133.3\ {\rm Wh}
\approx 2.13\ {\rm kWh}.
\]

As a check, the unclipped upper bound is the full 80% of incident energy:

\[
E_{\rm in}=\frac12(10\ {\rm h})(600\ {\rm W})=3000\ {\rm Wh}
\]

\[
E_{\rm upper}=0.8(3000)=2400\ {\rm Wh}=2.40\ {\rm kWh}.
\]

So clipping reduces the daily energy by

\[
2400-2133.3=266.7\ {\rm Wh},
\]

about \(11.1\%\).

\[
\boxed{E_{\rm daily}=2.133\ {\rm kWh}\approx 2.13\ {\rm kWh}}
\]

\[
\boxed{\text{Clipping begins at 10:20 AM and ends at 1:40 PM.}}
\]

\[
\boxed{\text{Unclipped upper bound}=2.40\ {\rm kWh};\ \text{clipped output is below it by }0.267\ {\rm kWh}.}
\]
